series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/2] mm: refactor find_next_best_node to find_next_best_node_in
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the find_next_best_node function to find_next_best_node_in, which takes an explicit candidates nodemask instead of always selecting from N_MEMORY. This change enables building fallback lists with non-N_MEMORY candidates without changing any existing functionality. The refactor is done by modifying three files: mm/internal.h, mm/memory-tiers.c, and mm/page_alloc.c. The patch has been reviewed and acknowledged by multiple kernel developers.

review_comments.author: David (Arm)
review_comments.summary: Reviewer David questioned the need for find_next_best_node_in() to take an explicit candidates nodemask, suggesting it could be sufficient to pass N_MEMORY as a candidate, and asked if other actual node masks are expected
review_comments.raw_body:
Just curious, for your use case, wouldn't it be enough to pass N_MEMORY?

Or do we expect to pass other actual node masks that are not derived from
node_states?


-- 
Cheers,

David

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged David's concern about the hardcoded N_MEMORY mask in find_next_best_node_in() and explained how the private node series will handle different zonelists, including a custom one built on a subset of N_MEMORY.
review_comments.raw_body:
That is the base case today - and in fact that's what's hard-coded
in the current logic.

For the private node series we will pass:

ZONELIST_FALLBACK:  N_MEMORY_GENERAL    /* general purpose nodes */

ZONELIST_PRIVATE:   N_MEMORY            /* All nodes, including private */

ZONELIST_KTEST:     (N_MEMORY_GENERAL ^ N_MEMORY)  /* private only */


the ZONELIST_KTEST is something i'm still working with - but it gives us
fully isolated pgdat structures that allow a KTEST to treat the node
mutations as determinstic and otherwise unreachable by the kernel
(because the kernel outside ktest can't select ZOENLIST_KTEST).


ANYWAY...

I don't expect us to build hundreds of these zonelists - they are
expensive to construct (space-wise), but that's largely because we
haven't needed to optimize it.

But you could imagine having a custom zonelist built on a subset
of N_MEMORY so that you could do like...

for_each_reclaimable_zone(z) {
	/* Reclaim */
}

and hide all this nasty zone business from other components of mm/ that
really don't need all that complexity (at most they want the LRUs).

~Gregory

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/2] mm/page_alloc: refactor build_node_zonelist() out of build_zonelists()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the code that builds zonelists in a node-ordered fashion, extracting it into a new function called build_node_zonelist(). This function takes a nodemask of candidate nodes and builds a zonelist for each selected node directly into the destination zonelist. The fallback order is printed as each node is added. The patch allows building new zonelists from candidate nodemasks instead of just the default N_MEMORY node state list, without introducing any functional changes.

review_comments.author: Zi Yan
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Zi Yan questioned the necessity for build_node_zonelist() to have a new zlidx parameter, suggesting it could reuse ZONELIST_FALLBACK like its predecessor build_zonelists_in_node_order().

Reviewer Zi Yan questioned the naming convention of build_node_zonelist(), pointing out that if build_thisnode_zonelists() implies ZONELIST_NOFALLBACK, then build_node_zonelist() should imply ZONELIST_FALLBACK.
review_comments.raw_body:
Why does build_node_zonelist() need to have a new zlidx instead of using
ZONELIST_FALLBACK like build_zonelists_in_node_order() did?

---

If build_thisnode_zonelists() means ZONELIST_NOFALLBACK, why
cannot build_node_zonelist() imply ZONELIST_FALLBACK?

review_comments.author: Zi Yan
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Zi Yan suggested renaming build_numa_aware_zonelist() to a more descriptive name, build_numa_aware_zonelist(), as the old comment mentioned 'NUMA-aware ordering of nodes' and the code uses find_next_best_node_in().
review_comments.raw_body:
Is build_numa_aware_zonelist() a better name? Since the old comment said
"NUMA-aware ording of nodes" and the code uses find_next_best_node_in().

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (author)
review_comments.summary:
Author agreed to use the new build_node_zonelist() function in two places instead of building a fallback list over N_MEMORY, confirming that the patch will need further revision.

Author acknowledged a misunderstanding about the GFP flag for zonelist selection, agreed that build_thisnode_zonelists() should be part of build_node_zonelist(), and suggested refactoring to simplify code.
review_comments.raw_body:
The intent is to build new zonelist over a set of candidate nodes, and
it's also just clearer: build ZONELIST_FALLBACK from N_MEMORY.

With this we get:

build_node_zonelists(pgdat, &node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON], ZONELIST_FALLBACK);
build_node_zonelists(pgdat, &node_states[N_MEMORY], ZONELIST_PRIVATE);
#ifdef PAGEALLOC_KTEST
nodemask_andnot(&private_only, &node_states[N_MEMORY],
		&node_states[N_MEMORY_COMMON]
build_node_zonelists(pgdat, &private_only, ZONELIST_KTEST);
#endif

---

thisnode actually means ZONELIST_X+1 as opposed to ZONELIST_NOFALLBACK.

Since folks are adamant about not allowing another GFP flag for zonelist
selection (beyond GFP_THISNODE), the result of this is that all future
zonelist additions must carry a FALLBACK + NOFALLBACK variant.

The question you actually want to ask is why build_thisnode_zonelists()
even exists - it should be part of build_node_zonelist()

I can probably follow up this series by just folding eveything into

/* build zlidx and zlidx+1 (nofallback) */
build_node_zonelists(pgdat, candidates, zlidx);

And add a BUILD_ON_BUG/ASSERT that forces any CONFIG_NUMA to have
balanced zonelist additions.

But I don't think it's strictly necessary for any of this, and we're
just shuffling code from one place to another.  Probably I can just add
that improvement when we add the next zonelist.  In the meantime - this
makes it easier to add new zonelists as-is (and just makes the code more
readable).

~Gregory

review_comments.author: Gregory Price (author)
review_comments.summary: Author acknowledged that the build_zonelists() function has been refactored to always use numa-aware ordering, and agreed that this is implied by the 'node' in the name of the new function build_node_zonelist().
review_comments.raw_body:
I think that's a vestige of older version having different ordering
options.  Now the zonelists are always numa aware (except for
!CONFIG_NUMA, which... duh). 

Anyway numa-aware is implied by "node" in the name.

But I don't have strong feelings about the name either way.

~Gregory

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch refactors the zonelist constructors and iterators in the Linux kernel to make them more flexible and modular. The existing behavior of picking nodes from N_MEMORY is made explicit, allowing callers to narrow the set of nodes used for fallback lists. A new function find_next_best_node_in() takes a candidate set as an argument, making it easier to build zonelists over specific sets of nodes. Additionally, the per-node construction loop in build_zonelists() is extracted into a separate function build_node_zonelist(), which can be parameterized on the candidate nodemask and destination zonelist index. These changes enable more flexible and efficient management of zonelists, particularly for generating private node zonelists.
